subject: brown tree snake
title: Half the Birds This Snake Kills Are Too Big for It to Eat

scenes.text: Half the birds this snake kills, it never gets to eat.
On Guam, scientists radio-tracked four hundred and sixty-one young starlings.
Brown tree snakes caused fifty-eight percent of their deaths.
But nearly half the time, the snake tried to swallow the bird and failed.
Its jaws couldn't fit. The birds were found dead on the ground, heads soaked in saliva.
No snake died trying. So it just keeps trying, killing birds it can't eat.

description:
On Guam, invasive brown tree snakes kill many young Micronesian starlings that turn out to be too big to swallow.
In a Virginia Tech and USGS study of 461 radio-tracked fledglings, snakes caused 58% of the deaths, and nearly half (about 48%) of their swallowing attempts failed, leaving the bird dead but uneaten.
No snake died from a failed attempt, so the attacks never stop.
Why do you think the snake attacks prey it can't swallow?
first_comment: The smallest snakes that succeeded swallowed birds weighing almost 80% of their own body. Would you have guessed snakes misjudge their prey this often?
